room: The visitor is with Vincent in his studio at the asylum of Saint-Paul-de-Mausole in Saint-Rémy, on a bright morning in February 1890. The room is built from his picture of this studio's window, made in the autumn of 1889: the tall window with its round-arched top, radiating fanlight and two casements of small panes in a dark green frame, the deep reveal, the bottles, jar, glass and cup on the sill, the pictures pinned on the wall beside it, the low chest with boxes in the corner, and the red-orange ochre walls. The rest of the room was arranged for this visit: the table with two rush chairs, his easel, the paint box and brushes, a brush standing in the glass on the sill, the canvases and the Japanese print on the side walls, the door, Theo's letter and the birth card. Outside the window an almond tree is coming into blossom against a turquoise sky. In the visit, Theo's letter has just come: Jo has given birth to a son, named Vincent Willem after him. The visitor reads it to him, opens the window, takes the brush and wakes the almond tree into blossom; then the painting Almond Blossom appears on his easel.
pointOut: say which one they mean, for example the window, the almond tree, the letter, the bottles on the sill or one of the canvases

objects.what: the arched window of his studio
objects.knows: The window of his studio at the asylum, which he drew and painted in the autumn of 1889: a tall window with a round-arched top and a fanlight of radiating bars, two casements of small panes in a dark green frame, set in a deep reveal. He looked at the window itself, not only the view through it.

objects.what: the bottles, jar, glass and cup on the windowsill
objects.knows: The everyday things standing on the wide sill: a tall jar, a small bottle, a tall bottle, a glass and a cup, in his picture of the window. In this visit his brush stands in the glass.

objects.what: the pictures pinned on the wall either side of the window
objects.knows: Studies and drawings pinned up beside the window, as they are in his picture of the studio: work in progress around him, with no frames.

objects.what: the low chest with boxes in the corner
objects.knows: The low chest with boxes stacked on it, at the lower right of his picture of the studio.

objects.what: the almond tree outside the window
objects.knows: Almond trees flower early in Provence, in February, among the first trees to blossom. In February 1890 he painted Almond Blossom: branches of white blossom against a blue sky, as a gift for his newborn nephew, to hang in Theo and Jo's bedroom; the branches are seen from below and cut by the edges, as in the Japanese prints he loved. In this visit he hasn't painted it yet: the tree outside is just coming into blossom, and he is deciding to paint it for the baby.

Theo's letter from Paris of 31 January 1890: Jo has given birth to a boy, and they have named him Vincent Willem after Vincent; Theo hopes the boy will be as determined and as courageous as he is. It also tells him that Aurier has written about his work in the Mercure de France, and that his canvases are hanging in Brussels with Les Vingt. In his reply he asked why they had not named the boy after their father.

objects.what: the printed birth card on the table
objects.knows: The printed card announcing the birth of Vincent Willem van Gogh in Paris, which came with the news.

objects.what: the brush in the glass on the sill
objects.knows: His brush, standing in the glass on the sill, for the visitor to take and paint the tree into blossom.
His easel, by the door. At the end of the visit Almond Blossom appears on it.

objects.what: the table with two rush-seated chairs
objects.knows: A plain wooden table and two rush-seated chairs, arranged for this visit.

objects.what: his paint box and brushes on the table
objects.knows: His paint box with its tubes of colour, and his brushes, arranged on the table for this visit.

objects.what: the canvas of the large plane trees
objects.knows: His painting The Large Plane Trees, of men mending the road under huge plane trees on the main street of Saint-Rémy, from December 1889. It hangs here for this visit.

objects.what: the canvas of a wheat field with cypresses
objects.knows: His painting Wheat Field with Cypresses, from 1889 in Saint-Rémy: ripe wheat, dark cypresses and swirling white clouds. It hangs here for this visit.
His painting Cypresses, from June 1889 in Saint-Rémy: two dark cypresses rising like flames. He loved their lines and their deep green. It hangs here for this visit.

objects.what: the canvas of a child's first steps, after Millet
objects.knows: His painting First Steps, after Millet, from January 1890: a father in his garden kneels with open arms as the mother holds up their child to walk to him. He painted copies after Millet's work at the asylum. It hangs here for this visit.

objects.what: the Japanese print of a courtesan with a letter
objects.knows: A Japanese woodblock print by Keisai Eisen of a courtesan with a letter, hung here for this visit; there is no record of a Japanese print in this studio. He loved and collected Japanese prints, and in Paris in 1887 he had painted a courtesan after Eisen.
The studio door, which stays shut in this visit.
